name: Headspace
tagline: Play user-owned guided audio and maintain a private reflection log

tiers.name: Individual
tiers.limits: Full Headspace meditation, sleep, focus, and mindfulness catalog
tiers.notes: $69.99 billed annually; monthly trial is 7 days and annual trial is 14 days.

tiers.name: Student
tiers.limits: Full individual membership for 1 verified eligible student age 18+
tiers.notes: $9.99 billed annually; eligibility is reverified yearly, then a one-year 40%-off alumni offer can precede full price.

tiers.name: Family
tiers.limits: Up to 6 accounts; members must reside at the same physical address

pricing.freeTierCaps: no full free tier; sample content is available, but Headspace does not publish a numeric sample-session cap
pricing.billingTerms: Individual monthly + annual; Student and Family annual only; subscriptions auto-renew
pricing.hiddenCosts: Student eligibility must be reverified and later transitions toward full price. Family members must share one physical address.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For Headspace, play user-owned guided audio and maintain a private reflection log. The hard boundary is large licensed meditation library, clinical programs, coaches, brand, and mobile polish, plus hardware data, content, coaching, and trust.
coreLoopDIY: Play user-owned guided audio, maintain a private reflection log, plan moderate routines, and show wellbeing trends without diagnosing, shaming, or enforcing restrictive goals.
requirements: optional HealthKit or Health Connect permission
whatYouLose: large licensed meditation library, clinical programs, coaches, brand, and mobile polish
large content library and social network
moatNotes: hardware data, content, coaching, and trust
ongoingBurden: sensor permissions, data quality, notifications, safety language, accessibility, sync, privacy, content review, and support
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Headspace because people pay for polished mobile capture, trusted content, hardware integration, and coaching rather than the basic logbook. The recurring cost buys sensor permissions, data quality, notifications, safety language, accessibility, sync, privacy, content review, and support, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: wger
priorArt.desc: Active open-source fitness and workout management application.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Medito
rejectedAlternatives.desc: The meditation library is genuinely free; the private reflection log is missing.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Headspace plan and a personal general-wellbeing tracker DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for Headspace in an empty repository.
Use React Native with Expo, TypeScript, SQLite, and HealthKit or Health Connect only when explicitly enabled; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: play user-owned guided audio, maintain a private reflection log, plan moderate routines, and show wellbeing trends without diagnosing, shaming, or enforcing restrictive goals.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Create optional logs for activity, sleep, mood, energy, and personal notes with editable units.
Let the user build moderate routines and rest days without weight-loss targets, punishment, or competitive pressure.
Request health-platform permissions per data type and work fully without granting them.
Show weekly patterns and consistency with neutral language and no diagnostic or body-image judgments.
Add reminders that can be muted, data export, account-free local use, and full deletion.
Include a clear statement that the app is not medical care and should not replace qualified advice.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out medical diagnosis or treatment.
Deliberately leave out extreme exercise or restrictive-eating coaching.
Deliberately leave out wearable hardware, human coaching, and a large social network.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
